concerns.analysis: On Page 3 of the source document, the phone number list includes '910-564-4194'. However, the output incorrectly transcribed this number as '910-564-7194', fabricating a different phone number.

concerns.description: Minor text differences beyond acceptable reformatting
concerns.analysis: In Section 8 (Funding Committee Report) on Page 5, the source document reads 'utilizing the PAT for discussion'. The output incorrectly transcribes this as 'utilizing the RAT for discussion', altering the meaning.

On page 3, a bordered box containing a simple vertical list of phone numbers is incorrectly extracted as a single-cell (1x1) data table. The guidelines explicitly state that single-column non-tabular content (such as a list or paragraphs) should not be rendered as a data table.
concerns.source_pdf_quote: A bordered box containing the text "Phone Numbers:" followed by 12 phone numbers on separate lines.

concerns.analysis: The source document contains a continuous numbered list of agenda items spanning multiple pages. While items 1 through 5, 7, and 8 were correctly extracted as `<ol>` list items, items 9, 10, 11, 12 (on page 6) and item 13 (on page 7) were extracted as plain text paragraphs. The guidelines explicitly state that numbered items must use list elements, not paragraphs containing numbered text.
concerns.source_pdf_quote: Numbered items starting with "9. Finance Team Report — Ms.Tapler...", "10. Standards Committee Report — Ms. Wright...", etc.
concerns.output_quote: {"type": "paragraph", "text": "**9. Finance Team Report** \u2014 Ms.Tapler has met with several PSAPs..."}

concerns.description: Output has more images than source PDF (ratio 1.3x) — possible image duplication
concerns.analysis: image_count_ratio=1.33. More images in output than in source indicates duplicated or fabricated image elements.

The source document uses underlining for several headings in the tables on Page 1 (e.g., 'Members Present via Teams', 'Staff Absent', 'Members Absent'). The output drops these underlines, substituting bold formatting but losing the original underline emphasis.
